posts.name: Ophidimancer
posts.cooked:
A question came up the other day when we had Mr Fixer in a fight against Plague Rat. Does Hoist Chain reduce Plague Rat's ability to do irreducible damage or does that not work because making someone do less damage counts as reducing their damage?

Or to put it in other words, is irreducible damage only irreducible at the point of impact, acting like armor piercing, or is it also irreducible at the source?
posts.raw:
A question came up the other day when we had Mr Fixer in a fight against Plague Rat. Does Hoist Chain reduce Plague Rat's ability to do irreducible damage or does that not work because making someone do less damage counts as reducing their damage?

Or to put it in other words, is irreducible damage only irreducible at the point of impact, acting like armor piercing, or is it also irreducible at the source?

posts.name: Drakossozh
posts.cooked: Irreducible damage is irreducible for all intents and purposes, so no, Hoist Chain would not reduce his damage :D
posts.raw: Irreducible damage is irreducible for all intents and purposes, so no, Hoist Chain would not reduce his damage :D

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Damage prevention, on the other hand, would work - best example there would be Resilient Hide (belonging to the Naturalist), provided Rat isn't buffed at all :).
posts.raw: Damage [i]prevention[/i], on the other hand, [i]would[/i] work - best example there would be Resilient Hide (belonging to the Naturalist), provided Rat isn't buffed at all :).

posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked: Interesting tidbit - the original printing of the game had Wraith's Stealth power "prevent" the next 2 damage she would take, so it stopped irreducible damage.  This is no longer true in the Enhanced Edition.
posts.raw: Interesting tidbit - the original printing of the game had Wraith's Stealth power "prevent" the next 2 damage she would take, so it stopped irreducible damage.  This is no longer true in the Enhanced Edition.

posts.name: JimmytheRat
posts.cooked: One of Bunker's incap powers does still prevent damage, however.  It, Undaunted, Resilient Hide, and Flak Jacket are the only prevention options for heroes I'm aware of.
posts.raw: One of Bunker's incap powers does still prevent damage, however.  It, Undaunted, Resilient Hide, and Flak Jacket are the only prevention options for heroes I'm aware of.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked: Immunity also prevents.  Flesh of the Sun God is the only immunity card I can think of at the moment, though.
posts.raw: Immunity also prevents.  Flesh of the Sun God is the only immunity card I can think of at the moment, though.

posts.name: Katsue
posts.cooked: Undaunted also prevents damage. Next Evolution and provides Immunity and Null Point Calibration Unit is effectively prevention.
posts.raw: Undaunted also prevents damage. Next Evolution and provides Immunity and Null Point Calibration Unit is effectively prevention.

posts.name: Flintlock
posts.cooked: See I was confused, because in my mind, applying a debuff to Plague Rat (the source of the irreducable damage) registers in my mind as "preventing" it from ever occurring, but I see your collective points.
posts.raw: See I was confused, because in my mind, applying a debuff to Plague Rat (the source of the irreducable damage) registers in my mind as "preventing" it from ever occurring, but I see your collective points.

posts.name: Humble-Knight
posts.cooked: In that case, so does the amulet
posts.raw: In that case, so does the amulet

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: If you mean the Amulet of the Elder Gods, redirection isn't the same as prevention - you're not stopping the damage from occurring, you're making it hit something else instead of yourself ;).
posts.raw: If you mean the Amulet of the Elder Gods, redirection isn't the same as prevention - you're not stopping the damage from occurring, you're making it hit something else instead of yourself ;).

posts.name: Humble-Knight
posts.cooked: Yeah I did and I agree but Donner brought up synaptic interruption which is a redirect as well
posts.raw: Yeah I did and I agree but Donner brought up synaptic interruption which is a redirect as well

posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked: There are pros and cons to redirection vs. prevention.  Redirection can be redirected right back (thanks, Iron Legacy. :( ) but it also provides a better outcome for the heroes (reduce damage to heroes, increase damage to villains, profit!).  But I see how it is derailing this thread as it is about damage reduction vs. irreducible vs. prevention, and redirection does not help the discussion at all.  Sorry for my seguay.
